en: Itivuttaka 12: Ekakanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said. In the First Chapter, there are ten discourses. In the Second Chapter, there are nine discourses. In the Third Chapter, there are eight discourses. In the Fourth Chapter, there are seven discourses. In the Fifth Chapter, there are six discourses. In the Sixth Chapter, there are five discourses. In the Seventh Chapter, there are four discourses. In the Eighth Chapter, there are three discourses. In the Ninth Chapter, there are two discourses. In the Tenth Chapter, there is one discourse. Thus, in the *Ekakanipāta*, there are fifty discourses in total. In the First Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Grateful 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Thankful 3. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Know 4. Discourse on the One Who Does Not See 5. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Understand 6. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Realize 7. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Attain 8. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Enter 9. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Abide 10. Discourse on the One Who Does Not Depart In the Second Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Grateful 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Thankful 3. Discourse on the One Who Knows 4. Discourse on the One Who Sees 5. Discourse on the One Who Understands 6. Discourse on the One Who Realizes 7. Discourse on the One Who Attains 8. Discourse on the One Who Enters 9. Discourse on the One Who Abides In the Third Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Wise 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Skillful 3. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Diligent 4. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Energetic 5. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Resolute 6. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Steadfast 7. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Firm 8. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Stable In the Fourth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Wise 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Skillful 3. Discourse on the One Who Is Diligent 4. Discourse on the One Who Is Energetic 5. Discourse on the One Who Is Resolute 6. Discourse on the One Who Is Steadfast 7. Discourse on the One Who Is Firm 8. Discourse on the One Who Is Stable In the Fifth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Noble 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Virtuous 3. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Wise 4. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Liberated 5. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Emancipated 6. Discourse on the One Who Is Not Released In the Sixth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Noble 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Virtuous 3. Discourse on the One Who Is Wise 4. Discourse on the One Who Is Liberated 5. Discourse on the One Who Is Emancipated 6. Discourse on the One Who Is Released In the Seventh Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Not a Stream-enterer 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Not a Once-returner 3. Discourse on the One Who Is Not a Non-returner 4. Discourse on the One Who Is Not an Arhat In the Eighth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the Stream-enterer 2. Discourse on the Once-returner 3. Discourse on the Non-returner 4. Discourse on the Arhat In the Ninth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is Not a Learner 2. Discourse on the One Who Is Not a Non-learner In the Tenth Chapter: 1. Discourse on the One Who Is a Learner 2. Discourse on the One Who Is a Non-learner Thus ends the *Ekakanipāta*. The total number of discourses is fifty. This concludes the second chapter of the first collection.
The Discourse on the Full Understanding of Anger.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

“Bhikkhus, one who does not directly know anger, does not fully understand it, does not cause dispassion toward it through the mind, and does not abandon it, is incapable of the destruction of suffering.”
“Monks, by directly knowing anger, fully understanding it, fading away from the mind toward it, and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. With regard to this, it is said:
“Having fully understood that anger by which beings, when provoked, go to an evil destination— ”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
